newsitem.title: USA: Texas corn harvest slows but still ahead of normal.
newsitem.headline: Texas corn harvest slows but still ahead of normal.

text.p: Statewide rains slowed fieldwork during the week to Sunday but corn harvesting progress remained slightly ahead of normal, the Texas agriculture statistics service said in a weekly crop upate.
Corn was 57 percent harvested, up only slightly from 54 percent a week earlier, but still above last year's 56 percent and the five-year average of 54 percent.
"Most producers were not complaining and were thankful for the moisture," the report said.
Corn was rated 65 percent good to excellent, up from just 49 percent a week earlier.
Sorghum harvesting was 57 percent complete, up from 55 percent a week earlier but slightly behind last year's 65 percent and the five-year average of 63 percent.
Sorghum was rated 55 percent good to excellent, up from 52 percent a week earlier.
Cotton was 13 percent harvested, up only marginally from 12 percent a week earlier and below last year and the five-year average of 16 percent.
It was rated 38 percent good to excellent, down from 48 percent a week earlier. "Cotton insect pressure was increasing in the Plains," the report noted.
